newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan stocks end down on record-high turnover.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan stocks end down on record-high turnover.

text.p: Conflicting signals from market officials, including a warning against stockbrokers giving public advice, sent Taiwan share prices gyrating to a lower close on Thursday as turnover rocketed to an all-time high.
The index once surged to as high as 8,827.88 points, a seven-year intraday high, but turned lower in late trade to close at 8,636.29, a loss of 77.20 points or 0.89 percent.
Thursday's intraday high eclipsed the seven-year high of 8,763.88 set on Tuesday.
Turnover soared to an all-time high T$251 billion, breaking the T$238.9 billion mark set on April 8.
The watchdog Securities and Exchange Commission said it had contacted brokerages to restate rules barring them from publicly forecasting market trends or recommending stock transactions.

A commission spokeswoman said stock brokers were allowed to forecast market trends and recommend stock trades to clients in their offices only, but clarified that "qualified analysts" in securities investment trust and investment consulting firms remained free to make market comment in public or the media.
The move came after the stock index rose on Wednesday for a fifth straight session was seen by many analysts as little more than a bid to cool the rallying market.

The commission caution contrasted with the comfort that brokers said investors took from comments made by central bank governor Sheu Yuan-dong after Wednesday's close. Stocks opened higher on Thursday on Sheu's assurance that the bank stood by its "stable to loose but not too loose" monetary policy.
Analysts noted that the securities commission's latest move echoed a similar caution in April that also was seen as a bid to cool off what then was a red-hot stock rally.
"Apparently the SEC again is trying to cool off the rallying market," said Nomura Securities research chief Ben Lee.
